question_text: Draw a standard Operational Amplifier (Op-Amp) configured for current sensing. What are its pros and cons, and what is its major source of error?
answer_text:
Pros: Large open-loop gain and often very low cost.
Cons: Low-side sensing only (V_CM ≈ GND), accuracy is set by external components, and single-ended inputs are highly vulnerable to PCB parasitics.
explanation_text: A standard op-amp is typically wired in a non-inverting configuration to measure a low-side shunt. Because it uses a single-ended input, any parasitic impedance in the PCB ground trace between the shunt and the true ground gets added directly to the measurement (V_shunt + V_p), causing significant error. Furthermore, because its inputs cannot survive high voltages, it is strictly limited to low-side sensing.
